My thoughts race, and I can’t stop talking, even if people look uncomfortable. I pace during calls, fidget with pens, can’t sit still. Then, just as suddenly, it fades.  

But more often, I’m just… empty. Getting out of bed takes everything. I’ve started crying at work—quietly, in the bathroom—over nothing. I stare at my computer and can’t focus. My mind feels like it’s drowning in thick fog. The motivation’s gone. I think, “What’s the point?” Sometimes I even think it would be easier if I weren’t here—no plan, just… a wish.  

A while back, something terrible happened—personal, but I don’t like to talk about it. It shook me. But these mood swings—they don’t always line up with memories of it. Sometimes I’m up when I should be down, irritable when I’ve had no trigger. It’s all jumbled. Like my nervous system doesn’t know whether to flee, fight, or collapse.

I did go through a traumatic event years ago, but my husband knows about that, and this recent rollercoaster—switching between crushing exhaustion and hyperactive surges—hasn’t been triggered by memories or flashbacks. I’ve been feeling like I’m on two completely different settings—sometimes I’m buzzing with energy, like I can design a whole campaign in one night and still have ideas left over. That happened for about a month last winter—I barely slept, not because I couldn’t, but because I just didn’t *want* to. My thoughts raced, I talked nonstop in meetings, even walked around the office without a reason, hands fidgeting. But I kept up with deadlines, so no one seemed worried.

Before that, though, things were heavy—really heavy—for over a year. I couldn’t enjoy anything, not even art, which has always been my thing. I’d lie in bed, exhausted just from breathing. There were moments, standing near the subway platform, where I’d get this sudden pull, like stepping forward would just… end the weight. No plan, just an urge. 

Something happened a few years back—something bad—but I don’t like to talk about it. I don’t know if it’s related. Sometimes I feel jumpy for no reason, other times I’m just numb. The highs and lows? I don’t know when they started, or why.

I’ve had these sudden, scary urges—like when I’m on the subway platform and this intense thought hits: *Just step forward*. No plan, no desire to die, but the impulse is strong and shocking.  

Before that, though, there was a month last winter where I was the opposite. I barely slept—like, three hours a night—but I didn’t care. I was designing constantly, starting six projects at once, reworking everything, pitching ideas nonstop. My speech felt so fast, like I couldn’t shut my thoughts off. I paced my apartment, couldn’t sit still, just tapping, fidgeting, talking to myself.  

Yeah, I went through something traumatic two years ago, but these mood swings don’t just follow that. The high-energy phase came out of nowhere, not triggered by any memory or stress. And then it just… faded. Now I’m back in the dark again.

I felt electric—like I didn’t need anything, couldn’t be quiet, had to talk, move, *do*. I paced a lot, couldn’t sit through meetings, just talked over people without meaning to. But that wasn’t really “me”—it faded, and then I crashed.  

Now I’m exhausted all the time. Getting out of bed feels impossible. I don’t enjoy design like I used to—it was my passion, now it’s just work. I have these sudden urges—standing on subway platforms, thinking about stepping forward, or walking toward traffic—not because I have a plan, but because the impulse just hits.  

The thing is, my sleep problems, the agitation, the jumpiness—they’ve been constant since the accident. I startle at noises, can’t relax. It’s not coming and going—it’s just *there*, tied to that memory.

I snapped at drivers one minute, then laughed like we were best friends the next.

My mind feels foggy, like I’m thinking through mud, and I’ve started believing I ruined my parents’ lives just by being born. I know that doesn’t make sense, but it feels true. I’ve even planned how I’d end things—when, where, maybe off a bridge near my apartment at night.  

Before this, though, around three weeks ago, it was the opposite. I was editing nonstop, jumping between projects, barely sleeping but buzzing with energy. I snapped at colleagues over small things—like a misplaced timeline or a sound edit—and felt restless, like I had to do ten things at once. But that wasn’t because of anything from my past—like that time in my early twenties when I witnessed that violent assault downtown. I still have the nightmares now and then, sure. But these mood swings—losing it over tiny mistakes, the sudden energy—those don’t connect to those memories. They just come and go, out of nowhere.
D009-D018_h019.question_b:
I’ve been having a really hard time since that train accident last year—I was on the platform when it happened, and I saw things I can’t unsee. Afterward, I couldn’t sleep, jumped at every sound, and stayed on edge constantly—like my body’s still back there. It never really let up.  

About three months ago, I hit this strange stretch where I was working 16 hours straight, editing nonstop, starting like five projects at once. I was snapping at coworkers over tiny things—totally unreasonable. But I wasn’t high or euphoric—just wound tight, irritable, like my nerves were exposed. It wasn’t a mood high—it just felt like trauma on overdrive. And then it faded back into this heavy fog.  

The last four months have been the worst. I can’t feel anything, not even films I used to love. My thinking’s slow, like wading through mud. I keep believing—*knowing*—that I could’ve stopped the accident, like I was meant to be on that train, like it’s my fault everyone died. Reality bends there—I know it doesn’t make sense, but it *feels* true. I’ve planned out how I’d do it—rope, the attic at my place, when no one’s around.  

The anger, the sleeplessness, the hyper-vigilance—they’re not coming and going randomly. They started *after* the trauma—and they’ve never really left.

D009-D018_h025.question_both: I’ve been feeling... off... for over a year now. Some days, I’m wired—practicing for hours past midnight, taking on extra gigs, barely sleeping but not even noticing because my head’s racing in this weird, restless way. My hands won’t stay still, and if someone gives a offhand comment about my playing, I snap—like last week when I yelled at a conductor over a tiny tempo shift. But then, it swings the other way. The last few months especially, I just feel hollow. Like no matter how many solos I nail or compliments I get, it means nothing. My arms feel like lead when I lift the violin, and I pace my apartment before concerts, wringing my hands even though I don’t want to. I’m exhausted all the time, even after naps. I had this one bad night a while back—something happened, I don’t like to talk about it—but I’m not sure if that’s connected. Sometimes I wonder if I’m just burnt out, or if this is something else. The energy comes and goes, the numbness stays.
D009-D018_h025.question_a:
I’ve been feeling off for a long time—like over a year now. There are days when I just feel empty, like nothing matters. I used to care about my playing, but now even nailing a tough passage doesn’t bring me joy. I pace during breaks, can’t sit still, even though I’m exhausted—my arms feel like lead after a concert. I haven’t touched my side projects in months.

But then there are these stretches—like three months last year—where sleep just didn’t matter. I’d stay up composing, practicing, even organizing my whole apartment at 3 a.m. I snapped at my section mate over a tiny tuning thing, which wasn’t like me, but I didn’t care. Felt restless, charged up, like I had five concerts in one day and loved it.

Yeah, I did go through a bad car accident years ago—sometimes I still get flashes—but these mood shifts? They don’t line up with trauma triggers. The irritability, the sleepless bursts—they come and go in waves, totally separate from that. It’s like my mood has its own unpredictable rhythm, not tied to the past. It’s the lows that wreck my work now.
D009-D018_h025.question_b: I’ve been feeling off for over a year now. Ever since the accident—my tour bus crashed, and I saw people die—I can’t quiet my mind. I jump at loud sounds, like a cymbal crash during rehearsal, and sometimes I blankly find myself in the middle of playing a passage, drenched in sweat. I’ve had these moments of being wired—lasted a few months—where I’d practice 10 hours straight, start arranging pieces, even book gigs nonstop. I didn’t sleep for nights but didn’t feel tired. I snapped at my conductor over tiny mistakes. But it wasn’t mania, I don’t think—it felt like my body was always on edge, like I was still running from the crash. Even when that phase passed, the rest stayed. I sit in my apartment for hours, numb. My arms feel like lead when I lift the violin. I used to care about auditions, solos—now it’s like nothing matters. I pace, can’t sit during concerts, wring my hands until the skin cracks. That hyped-up edge? It never really left. It’s always there, since that day.
